To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the historical trajectory of access and equity policies for African American students in higher education is characterized by a series of progressive and regressive policy initiatives, and (2) the progressive and regressive policies were shaped by the dominant racial ideology of white supremacy and its racist ideologies, and by the counter-hegemonic ideologies of African Americans.
African Americans have been systematically excluded from higher education since its inception, and that the policies that have been put into place to remedy this exclusion have been inadequate.

(a) African American students have made great strides in higher education since the 1965 Higher Education Act was passed; (b) African American students are still underrepresented and underachieving; and (c) African American students face a myriad of barriers to access and success in higher education.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which the historical context of race relations in the United States has shaped and continues to shape policies that impact the enrollment and degree attainment of African Americans.
the following questions: What are the historical and current policies that have impacted access and equity for African American students in higher education?
the following questions: What policies have been put in place to address African American student underrepresentation in higher education?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
African American students have been systematically denied equal access and equity in the higher education system.
the history of policy making in higher education has been a story of progress and regression.
the policies of the past have not worked to improve African American student access and success in higher education.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
African Americans have made great progress, but that the struggle is far from over.
African American students have not fared well in the higher education arena.
the United States has not been a nation that has been willing to invest in African American students and has instead been willing to invest only when it is in the interest of white supremacy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
African American students continue to be marginalized in the higher education system.
African American students are still not fully included in the American dream and the promise of higher education.
the current policy environment is not conducive to the advancement of African American students in higher education.
